kaigo-gap-reserve-check.heading: Check whether emergency supplies are actually usable
paragraphs: Supplies in a bag are not necessarily usable when needed. Follow facility inspection methods to check whether flashlights and radios have suitable batteries or power and actually work. If responsible staff do not know storage locations, retrieving them may take time.

Cash and necessary documents can help access support or establish needed information during disasters. Prepare and manage them according to facility plans and responsibilities. Do not leave money or personal information freely accessible for anyone to take.

Preparations differ individually. Check with the person and responsible staff about mobility aids, hearing-aid supplies, routine-care items and current medicines. One shared bag does not establish that everyone’s needs are met.

Alongside names and quantities, record unusable conditions, missing items, the person responsible for replenishment and the next check. Expired or incompatible stock is not usable preparation even if counted. Communicate uninspected items separately as unconfirmed.

Learning example: a radio is in the bag, but the stored batteries are incompatible. Backup supplies for a hearing-aid user also remain unchecked. Do not end the inspection at ‘radio present.’ Hand over battery incompatibility separately from unconfirmed individual supplies.

These examples do not prescribe identical items or quantities for every facility. Actual stock follows the disaster plan and personal needs. Check medicines with responsible staff or healthcare professionals; a learned list alone does not justify changing types or amounts.

kaigo-gap-body-direction.heading: Read left and right from the person’s body
paragraphs: Describe body right and left from the person’s viewpoint. When facing them, their right appears on the worker’s left. Rather than saying only ‘this side,’ identify the reference, such as ‘the person’s right side.’

In the large intestine, the ascending colon normally travels upward on the right side of the person’s abdomen. The transverse colon continues across, and the descending colon travels down the left side. Do not confuse the viewing direction with anatomical names.

In learning, compare the diagram with the relationship from the person’s lower right abdomen upward, across to the left and then down the left. This practices anatomical orientation. Understanding arrows does not establish abdominal pressure, duration, repetitions or conditions permitting a technique.

For abdominal pain or similar complaints, record location, onset and personal words and tell healthcare professionals or the training supervisor. Diagram direction alone does not determine cause or authorize a procedure applying force to the abdomen.

Information such as pregnancy, inflammatory bowel disease, abdominal surgery or wounds also matters when consulting about support. These alone do not determine whether a technique is appropriate; check a suitable response with professionals. This lesson teaches orientation and terms.

kaigo-gap-anatomy-terms.heading: Distinguish scrotum, testes and foreskin
paragraphs: The scrotum is the external sac surrounding the testes; testes are glands within that sac. The outer sac and internal organs differ, so do not use one name for both when describing an observed area.

The foreskin is skin covering the glans at the penis’s tip. It differs from the scrotum and testes. If an instruction’s terminology is unclear, check which area and action it concerns. Similar-looking names do not justify applying the same movement.

Do not guess pulling direction or force and proceed while explanations remain unclear. If the target area is unknown, do not start the unconfirmed movement; ask the training supervisor or healthcare professional. If there is pain or resistance, avoid forcing continuation and report the condition.

Respect embarrassment and privacy when consulting. Avoid unnecessary exposure in public or spreading information to uninvolved people. Tell necessary recipients separately the confirmed area, personal words and unconfirmed content.

This lesson checks anatomical names and the principle of not turning unclear instructions into actions. The original source’s male wiping movement has not been established here as a safe technique. Check individual genital-hygiene procedures through professional guidance and facility methods.

kaigo-depth-qol-outcome.heading: Consider quality of life through personal experience
paragraphs: QOL means quality of life. It includes emotional richness such as satisfaction, happiness and purpose. Many completed staff tasks alone do not show whether the person’s life has improved.

In reviewing an activity, check its meaning to the person as well as what happened and how often. Listen to statements such as ‘I enjoyed it’ or ‘There was little chance to talk,’ without substituting staff preferences or satisfaction for personal evaluation.

Separate doing an action independently from choosing and deciding. Someone needing help moving a hand may still choose the activity, participation time and desired role. Assistance quantity alone does not establish satisfaction or wishes.

Learning example: after sorting photographs, the person says, ‘We sorted more, but I wanted time to talk about the memories.’ The number sorted and desired time are separate information. Ask again how they want to spend time and which parts they want to do together.

If the activity does not fit, record current wishes and participation difficulties and tell the team. Do not increase activity numbers merely to improve the appearance of records. Review support considering wishes, abilities and safety together.

Do not diagnose psychological condition or independently change a care plan from one reply or activity count. This lesson practices checking personal experience and communicating it as information for reviewing support.

kaigo-depth-community-choice.heading: Support chosen participation in the community
paragraphs: Community or group participation requires opportunities to express wishes and choose how to join. Bringing everyone to one place is insufficient if attendance is unwanted or usable participation methods are unavailable.

People receiving care can contribute experience and strengths rather than only receive help. Ask what role they want as well as what they want done for them. Needing support does not establish inability to contribute.

If a participation method does not fit, check the difficulty together. Discuss methods and necessary support to use wishes and abilities. Do not demand the same method from everyone or exclude someone solely because one part is difficult.

Learning example: someone who enjoys recorded books wants to introduce one at a community gathering. Restricting presentations to independent text readers would prevent sharing that experience. Ask how they want to present and discuss necessary preparation and arrangements.

This does not mean every activity fits everyone equally. Adjust actual participation after checking wishes, abilities, necessary support and venue or organizational conditions. Consult the person and responsible staff rather than letting staff views alone determine participation.

kaigo-depth-service-location.heading: Distinguish services by location and use
paragraphs: To distinguish basic care services, check where support is received and who travels where. Separate home-visit services, where staff visit the person’s home; day services, where the person attends a facility; and residential services, where they live at a facility.

Home-visit care provides support at home. Day care is an example of attending during daytime for support. Residential services provide support while the person lives there. Connect names to living settings and how support is received rather than memorizing names alone.

A transport vehicle or care workers alone do not determine service type. Check the support location, whether the person returns home afterward and whether they live at the facility. Avoid judging everything from one cue.

One person’s needs may change by period or time of day. For handovers of actual plans, organize confirmed person, date/time, place and support details, and communicate undecided points separately. A type name alone does not finalize a schedule.

This classification explains settings and delivery methods, not personal eligibility, insurance benefits, prices or facility suitability. For actual coordination, check wishes and consult the responsible person, care manager or other appropriate professional.

kaigo-depth-care-evaluation.heading: Separate provided support from goal achievement
paragraphs: A care plan links the life the person wants with specific goals and support. Staff actions alone do not reveal the personal outcome being sought. Check the relationship between wishes, goals and support.

Implementation records show whether planned assistance occurred. Responses and activity outcomes inform whether goals were approached. The number of staff invitations cannot directly prove personal goal achievement.

Learning example: the goal is independent choice of an afternoon activity. Staff offered guidance three times, but the person says, ‘I don’t know what I can choose.’ Three explanations record implementation. Without evidence of understanding and choice, that alone cannot establish goal achievement.

If expected outcomes are not reached, review as a team whether information was missing, explanation or participation conditions fit, and the goal itself suited the person. Do not attribute the result to inadequate personal effort; use personal words and observed facts.

Evaluation aims to reconsider suitable support, not increase scores or counts. Record actions, responses and unknowns separately and share with the person and responsible staff. Consult about actual goal or assistance changes rather than deciding alone.

162.title: Check whether emergency supplies are actually usable
objectives: Communicate individual uncertainties in a way that leads to replenishment responsibilities and rechecking.
162.context: Learn disaster-supply inspection and handovers. This lesson does not prescribe uniform supply types or quantities.
162.artCaption: Workers check disaster supplies. Distinguish presence from usability when needed.

163.title: Read left and right from the person’s body
objectives: Explain colon locations using the person’s right and left.
Distinguish understanding anatomy diagrams from deciding to perform techniques.
163.context: Practice communicating body orientation separately from actual symptom assessment or massage practice.
163.artCaption: Listen to personal words and check body locations. This picture does not show colon orientation or abdominal massage.

164.title: Distinguish scrotum, testes and foreskin
objectives: Distinguish meanings of scrotum, testes and foreskin.
Clarify unclear movements without guessing, while protecting dignity.
164.context: Learn anatomical terms and how to clarify. This text alone does not teach practical genital wiping.
164.artCaption: Clean supplies are prepared. The picture cannot establish genital-washing or tissue-movement methods.

165.title: Consider quality of life through personal experience
objectives: Separate activity amount from personal meaning and satisfaction.
Support choices for people needing help and connect wishes to reviewing support.
165.context: Practice evaluating outcomes beyond staff workload. Check the way the person values spending time.
165.artCaption: Listen while looking at photographs and check what matters through the person’s own words.

166.title: Support chosen participation in the community
objectives: Respect choices and desired community roles for people receiving care.
Discuss support with the person according to participation difficulties.
166.context: Consider participation through choices, roles and suitable conditions, beyond merely being in the same place.
166.artCaption: People participate in activities. Consider suitable participation without requiring identical tools or methods.

167.title: Distinguish services by location and use
objectives: Distinguish home-visit, day and residential services through support and living settings.
Do not confuse type names with confirmed schedules or eligibility.
167.context: Learn basic delivery methods, not insurance eligibility or judging a personally suitable facility.
167.artCaption: Scenes show home visits, attendance elsewhere and facility living. Distinguish services by location and use.

168.title: Separate provided support from goal achievement
objectives: Record staff support separately from personal goal achievement.
Avoid assuming why results differ; connect with evaluation by the person and team.
168.context: Practice distinguishing implementation from evaluation through specific information. Counts alone do not establish goals.
168.artCaption: The person and worker discuss records. Review the plan by separating support provided from personal responses.

weekly-kaigo-gap-reserve-check-probe.prompt: A disaster-supply radio has incompatible batteries, and backup supplies for a hearing-aid user remain unchecked. Which handover is appropriate?
options: Record the radio and batteries as usable because the radio exists.
Record unchecked individual supplies as unnecessary.
Remove only unusable items without deciding replenishment or rechecking.
Separate incompatible batteries from unchecked individual supplies and confirm replenishment responsibility and rechecking plans.
rationales: Equipment without compatible power cannot be treated as usable.
Unconfirmed is not unnecessary. Individual needs still require checking.
Removing shortages does not restore usable preparation. Connect replenishment with the next check.
This separates confirmed incompatibility from unconfirmed needs and connects responsibilities with next checks.

weekly-kaigo-gap-body-direction-probe.prompt: Facing the person, a worker calls the abdomen on the worker’s left ‘the person’s left.’ Which correction is appropriate?
options: Change bodily right/left labels according to where the worker stands.
Check sides from the person’s body: ascending colon normally on the right, descending on the left.
Avoid identifying a reference and use only ‘this side.’
Treat understanding diagram arrows as confirming conditions permitting abdominal contact.
rationales: Anatomical sides use the person as reference, not the worker’s position.
Facing one another reverses apparent sides. This checks usual colon locations from the person’s viewpoint.
‘This side’ alone leaves the viewpoint unclear. State the reference.
Arrows teach spatial relationships, not suitability or methods for techniques.

weekly-kaigo-gap-anatomy-terms-probe.prompt: A study memo treats scrotum and testes as identical and says ‘pull’ without a clear target. Which correction is appropriate?
options: Distinguish scrotum as the outer sac, testes as glands inside, and foreskin as glans-covering skin. Do not perform unclear actions; check with professionals.
Their proximity means either name indicates the same movement.
Knowing definitions establishes the action’s target and method too.
An action appearing in the memo means it is verified and can be taught to others.
rationales: This distinguishes the three areas without justifying an unconfirmed movement from terminology alone.
Nearby locations still involve different external and internal structures. Names are not interchangeable.
Definitions differ from checking an instruction’s target and safe method. The action remains unconfirmed.
Written content does not establish a verified safe technique. Do not pass on ambiguous movements unchanged.

weekly-kaigo-depth-qol-outcome-probe.prompt: More photograph albums were completed, but the person says, ‘I wanted time to talk about the memories.’ Which QOL evaluation is appropriate?
options: More albums conclusively establish higher satisfaction.
Exclude personal choice because assistance was needed.
Record album counts separately from personal experience, ask desired time use and participation, and review support.
Do not record personal words because satisfaction cannot be judged externally.
rationales: Album numbers are task outcomes but cannot establish satisfaction or purpose alone.
Assistance needs do not remove self-determination. Check choices.
This separates activity amount from personal meaning and reviews support through wishes.
Avoiding staff assumptions does not mean ignoring personal words. Record them as important evaluation information.

weekly-kaigo-depth-community-choice-prob.prompt: Someone enjoying recorded books wants to introduce one at a community gathering. The organizer considers presentations only for independent text readers. What is appropriate?
options: Restrict people needing support to listening regardless of wishes.
Ask how the person wants to present and discuss participation using their experience and necessary preparation.
Bringing everyone to the same venue removes any need to check methods.
Require identical reading ability before considering participation methods.
rationales: Receiving support and contributing experience or a role are compatible. Check wishes.
This uses wishes and abilities and discusses suitable conditions.
Venue presence does not guarantee participation in the desired way.
A single required method can overlook experience and opportunities to participate.

weekly-kaigo-depth-service-location-prob.prompt: A plan lists 1 staff visiting home,2 the person attending a facility by day and returning home, and 3 support while living at a facility. Which classification and handover is appropriate?
options: 1 day service,2 home visit,3 residential; knowing types removes date/time checks.
Care workers are present in all three, so settings need not differ.
1 home visit,2 day,3 residential; names alone establish eligibility and fees.
Distinguish 1 home visit,2 day and 3 residential, and separately confirm actual dates/times, places and support details.
rationales: Who travels in 1 and 2 is reversed. Type alone also does not confirm timing.
Support and living locations matter, not staff presence alone.
Classification is correct but does not establish personal eligibility or charges.
This separates delivery methods and treats confirmed plans for coordination separately.

weekly-kaigo-depth-care-evaluation-probe.prompt: The goal is personal choice of an afternoon activity. Staff explained three times, but each time the person said they did not understand the choices. Which evaluation is appropriate?
options: Three explanations establish goal achievement.
Conclude that inadequate personal effort caused the lack of choice.
Separate explanations from the unmet outcome and review explanation, participation conditions and goal suitability with the person and team.
Because explanation counts can be recorded, exclude personal responses from evaluation.
rationales: Explanation counts show staff actions, not understanding and choice.
Unconfirmed factors include explanation and conditions, so personal effort cannot be blamed.
This separates implementation and outcome and reconsiders personally suitable goals and support.
Personal responses are essential information for assessing whether support advanced the goal.
